issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires Farm to store animals in a List implemented with an ArrayList and to initialize that ArrayList in the no-argument constructor. The solution implementation instead uses a Queue<Animal> backed by a LinkedList. This is a structural mismatch between the specification and the provided solution reference and may confuse students who follow the textual instruction (expecting List/ArrayList) but inspect the solution (which uses Queue/LinkedList).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent with the problem statement. Either update the solution to use List<Animal> animals = new ArrayList<>(); (and update getter/setter signatures and imports accordingly) or relax/change the problem text to allow a Queue/LinkedList implementation. Preferably change the solution to use List/ArrayList to match the explicit instruction in the problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires the farm's animal collection to be a List initialized as an ArrayList (getter/setter for that List). The solution instead declares the same conceptual attribute as a Queue<Animal> and initializes it with a LinkedList. This mismatch in the identifier/type used for the central 'animals' collection (List/ArrayList vs Queue/LinkedList) creates a mapping confusion for students: the problem and template instruct use of List/ArrayList and expect corresponding getter/setter signatures, while the reference solution presents a differently-named/typed collection and different usage (offer/Queue semantics).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement and template by using the same collection type and identifiers: declare the attribute as List<Animal> animals, initialize it as new ArrayList<> in the no-arg constructor, and provide getter/setter with List<Animal> signatures. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template instructions to accept Queue/LinkedList consistently if Queue semantics are intended.
